title: View, edit, or delete draft orders
page_summary: The Drafts page lists orders you've started on behalf of customers but haven't turned into real orders yet. You can reopen a draft to change it, or remove drafts you no longer need. A draft becomes a regular order on the Orders page once payment is accepted.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders → Drafts.
2. Click the draft order you want to work on.
3. To change it, update details such as products, customer, shipping, tags, or payment terms, then click Save.
4. To remove it, click Delete draft order and confirm by clicking Delete draft order again in the dialog.
5. Note: deleting a completed draft does not remove the order that was created from it, and drafts created on or after April 1, 2025 are removed automatically after a year without any edits.
keywords: drafts, draft orders, draft list, delete draft, edit draft, saved orders, unfinished orders, quotes

title: View and recover abandoned checkouts
page_summary: Abandoned checkouts are checkouts where a customer entered an email address but didn't finish paying within about ten minutes. This page lets you review them, see whether a recovery email was sent, and whether the checkout was later recovered. Records older than three months are removed automatically.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders → Abandoned checkouts.
2. Click the checkout number you want to look at.
3. To send a recovery link yourself, click the customer's email address in the customer information; your email program opens with the recovery link included. Only send it to that customer, because anyone with the link can complete the checkout.
4. To send recovery emails automatically, go to Apps → Messaging → Automations, open the actions menu on the Abandoned checkout emails by Shopify automation, choose Edit settings, turn on automatic sending, pick the recipients and delay, then click Save.
5. Back on the Abandoned checkouts page, check the Email status and Recovery status columns to track results.
keywords: abandoned cart, abandoned checkout, recover cart, cart recovery email, incomplete checkout, lost sales, unfinished purchase

title: Edit an order after it's placed
page_summary: Order editing lets you change an order after purchase but before it's fulfilled, without cancelling and recreating it. You can add or remove products, change quantities, add custom items, and adjust shipping fees or item discounts. Some orders can't be edited, such as local delivery, Shop Pay Installments, or orders created by apps.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and click the order.
2. Click Edit.
3. Make your changes: click Product to add an existing product, click Custom item to add a one-off item, type a new number in the Quantity column, or hover over an item and click × to remove it.
4. For removed or reduced items, leave Restock units selected to return stock to inventory, or deselect it to skip restocking. Optionally add an internal Reason for edit.
5. Review the new order total, save the update, and choose whether to notify the customer.
6. If the total went down, issue a refund afterwards; if it went up, collect the balance by sending an invoice or accepting payment.
keywords: edit order, change order, modify order, add item to order, remove item, change quantity, update order, order editing

title: Cancel an order
admin_page: Orders → (open the order) → More actions → Cancel order
page_summary: Cancelling an order marks it as stopped so nobody keeps processing or fulfilling it, and lets you refund, restock, and notify the customer in one step. Partially fulfilled orders can't be cancelled; you'd need to cancel the fulfillment first or use refunds and returns.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and click the order.
2. Click More actions → Cancel order.
3. Under Refund payment, choose Original payment method, Store credit, or Later (use Later for partial refunds or if the order was already refunded).
4. Pick a reason from the Reason for cancellation menu and optionally add a staff note.
5. Decide whether to keep Restock inventory and Send a notification to the customer selected (both are on by default).
6. Click Cancel order. To cancel up to 250 orders at once, select them on the Orders page and use the bulk Cancel orders action, but be careful: bulk cancel may refund immediately, including orders already refunded.
keywords: cancel order, void order, cancel purchase, stop order, bulk cancel, cancel and refund

title: Create a return or exchange
page_summary: Returns let you record items a customer is sending back, with a reason, optional fees, and return shipping, and optionally add replacement items as an exchange. Only fulfilled items that haven't been refunded can be returned. Create the return before refunding so the reason is recorded.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and open the order.
2. Click Return (if the order still has unfulfilled items, it's under More actions → Return).
3. Enter the quantity of each item coming back and choose a return reason.
4. Optionally add a restocking fee or return shipping fee in the Summary section, and add exchange items by clicking Add products under Exchange items.
5. Choose a return shipping option: create a return label in Shopify (US only), upload your own label, or no shipping required.
6. Click Create return. When the items arrive, process the return, then refund the customer, collect any balance owed, or fulfill the exchange items.
keywords: return, returned order, order returned, handle a return, exchange, swap item, customer return, return label, restocking fee, send back, replacement

title: Understand order, payment, and fulfillment statuses
page_summary: Every order shows an order status (Open, Archived, Canceled), a payment status, and a fulfillment status, plus a return status if a return exists. These labels tell you what work is left on the order, such as collecting money or shipping items.
steps:
1. Payment statuses: Pending (still processing or paid later/manually), Authorized (approved but not yet captured), Due (past the payment-terms date), Expired (authorization lapsed without capture), Paid, Partially paid, Refunded, Partially refunded, and Voided (authorization released before capture). An Expiring badge warns two days before an authorization deadline.
2. Fulfillment statuses: Unfulfilled, In progress (being picked/packed), On hold (paused, stock stays reserved), Scheduled (prepaid subscription waiting for its date), Partially fulfilled, Fulfilled, and Fulfillment not required (shown as Not required).
3. Order statuses: Open means work is still pending, Archived means it was closed manually or automatically, Canceled means it was cancelled.
4. Return statuses: Return requested, Return in progress, Inspection complete, and Returned.
5. Use the filters on the Orders page (for example, Payment status) to find orders in a particular state.
keywords: order status, payment status, fulfillment status, what does authorized mean, pending, unfulfilled, partially paid, voided, on hold, status meaning

title: Archive an order
page_summary: Archiving closes an order that needs no more work so it moves out of your open orders and into the Closed view. By default, Shopify archives orders automatically once they're paid and fulfilled or fully refunded; you can turn that off in Settings → General under Order processing.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders.
2. Click the order number you want to archive.
3. Click More actions, then click Archive orders.
4. The order's status changes to Archived and it appears in the Closed view.
5. To archive or unarchive many orders at once, select them on the Orders page and use a bulk action.
keywords: archive order, close order, hide order, closed orders, unarchive, auto archive, completed orders

title: Print packing slips
admin_page: Orders → (open or select orders) → Print → Print packing slips
page_summary: Packing slips list the items going into a shipment so you can pack and include them in the box. You can print them for one order or for many orders at once. If an order ships in several packages, each shipment gets its own slip.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders.
2. For one order, click the order; for several, tick the checkboxes next to the orders you need.
3. Click Print, then Print packing slips.
4. If you have more than one location, pick the fulfilling location and click Continue.
5. Print the slips or save them.
6. To change how slips look, edit the packing slip template under Settings → Shipping and delivery in the Documents area.

title: Buy and print a shipping label
admin_page: Orders → (open the order) → Unfulfilled section → Create shipping label
page_summary: You can buy carrier shipping labels directly from an unfulfilled order and print them along with packing slips or customs forms. Your fulfillment location must be eligible for Shopify shipping labels; if not, use a shipping label app instead.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and open an order with unfulfilled items.
2. In the Unfulfilled section, click Create shipping label.
3. Confirm the items and their weight; for international orders, click Edit customs information and add the country of origin and HS code.
4. Choose a package, check the total weight, and select a shipping service (plus any extras like signature confirmation or insurance).
5. Choose a ship date and whether to email tracking details to the customer.
6. Click Buy shipping label, then print the label along with packing slips or customs forms if you want them.

title: Add notes and timeline comments to an order
page_summary: Each order has a Notes section and a Timeline where staff can leave internal information. The timeline also records events like payments, edits, and refunds. Notes and comments are for staff only and aren't shown to the customer.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and click the order.
2. To add or change a note, click the pencil icon in the Notes section, type your note, and click Save.
3. To add a comment, scroll to the Timeline section, click Leave a comment..., type your message, and click Post.
4. Use the timeline to review the order's history, such as payment events.
keywords: order note, add note, comment, timeline, internal note, staff note, order history, order activity

title: Review an order's fraud risk
page_summary: Fraud analysis helps you decide whether an order is safe to fulfill. It shows fraud indicators (such as address and CVV checks, location, and repeated card attempts) and, for eligible online card orders, an overall recommendation of low, medium, or high risk. Medium- and high-risk orders show a warning symbol on the Orders page.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders; look for the warning symbol next to risky orders.
2. Click the order and find the Order risk section.
3. Open the risk details to see the recommendation and the individual indicators.
4. Act on the overall recommendation rather than any single indicator: fulfill if low risk, confirm with the customer if it says to investigate, or consider cancelling and refunding if it's high risk.
5. Avoid fulfilling high-risk orders, since chargebacks can put your payment processing at risk.
keywords: fraud, risk, high risk order, fraud analysis, suspicious order, chargeback, order risk, fraudulent

title: Put an order's fulfillment on hold
admin_page: Orders → (open the order) → Unfulfilled section → Mark as on hold
page_summary: Holding fulfillment pauses shipping on an order, for example when fraud risk is high or stock isn't available, while keeping its inventory reserved. On-hold orders don't show in the Unfulfilled list until the hold is released.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and click the order.
2. In the Unfulfilled or In progress section, open the drop-down and click Mark as on hold.
3. Choose the items to hold and pick a reason from the Hold reason menu.
4. Click Mark as on hold.
5. To release it later, open the order and click Release hold in the On hold section (if there are several holds, choose which to release, then click Release).
keywords: hold fulfillment, on hold, pause order, pause shipping, release hold, delay fulfillment, stop shipping

title: Export orders to CSV
page_summary: Exporting creates a CSV file of your orders, or just their transaction histories, for spreadsheets or record keeping. Small exports download straight away; larger exports or date-range exports are emailed to you and the store owner.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders.
2. Filter and sort the list so it shows the orders you want.
3. Click Export.
4. In the Export orders window, choose which orders to include (for example, orders by date with a start and end date) and pick the file format.
5. Click Export orders for full order data, or Export transaction histories for captured payment details only.
6. Up to 50 orders download directly; bigger exports arrive by email.

title: Capture payment for an authorized order
page_summary: If your store uses manual capture, card payments are first authorized (money reserved) and you must capture them to actually collect the funds. Authorizations expire (Shopify Payments allows 7 days for cards), so capture before the deadline. Capturing changes the payment status from Authorized to Paid.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders; filter by Payment status: Authorized to find orders waiting for capture.
2. Click the order number.
3. Click Capture payment.
4. Optionally lower the amount to capture only part of the payment (you can't capture more than was authorized).
5. Click Capture.
6. To capture the full amount on several card orders at once, select them on the Orders page and use a bulk action.
keywords: capture payment, authorized, collect payment, manual capture, authorization expiring, charge card, partial capture

title: Mark an order as paid
admin_page: Orders → (open the order) → Payment pending → Collect payment → Mark as paid
page_summary: Mark as paid is for orders with a pending payment where you've already received the money outside Shopify, such as cash or bank transfer. Shopify records the order as paid without charging anyone, and the customer gets an order confirmation email.
steps:
1. In the Shopify admin, go to Orders and click the order.
2. In the Payment pending section, click Collect payment.
3. Click Mark as paid.
4. If you haven't actually received the money yet, use Send invoice from the same Collect payment menu instead, so the customer can pay through checkout.
keywords: mark as paid, paid manually, cash payment, bank transfer, pending payment, record payment, manual payment, collect payment

title: Search, filter and save views on the Products list
page_summary: The Products page lists every product in your store, 50 per page. You can search, filter, sort and change columns to find products, and save combinations of filters as reusable views. Built-in views are All, Active, Draft and Archived.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products.
2. To search, type words into the Search and filter field and press Enter. Matches come from product titles, descriptions and tags.
3. To filter, pick a filter, then choose an operator and a value. Products must match every filter you add.
4. To sort, click the columns (layout) icon and choose an option from the Sort by menu. On desktop, the sort resets when the list refreshes.
5. To keep a set of filters, click Save, name the view, then click Create view. Sort order isn't stored in views.

title: Edit an existing product
page_summary: Each product has a details page where you can change its title, description, media, pricing, inventory, shipping, variants and organization. Saved changes show up in your online store right away.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products.
2. Click the name of the product you want to change.
3. Update the details you need, such as the title, description, price or tags.
4. Click Save.

title: Duplicate a product
admin_page: Products → (product name) → More actions → Duplicate product
page_summary: Duplicating creates a new, separate product based on an existing one, without changing the original. It's useful for similar items. If you only need size or color options, Shopify suggests using variants instead.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product you want to copy.
2. Click More actions, then Duplicate product.
3. Enter a title for the copy and, optionally, choose which details to carry over.
4. Choose a status for the copy: draft, active or unlisted. An active copy goes to the same sales channels as the original, so pick draft if you want to choose channels first.
5. Click Duplicate product.
keywords: duplicate product, copy product, clone product, make a copy, similar product

title: Product status: Active, Draft, Archived and Unlisted
page_summary: A product's status controls whether it can be sold. Active means it's ready to sell. Draft means it still needs work. Archived means it's no longer sold and is hidden from your store and the main product list. Unlisted products can be bought only through their direct link and are hidden from search, collections, recommendations and your sitemap.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products.
2. Click the product you want to update.
3. In the Status section, choose Active, Draft or Unlisted from the drop-down.
4. Click Save.
5. If the product is archived, unarchive it first. It comes back as a draft, and then you can change its status.

title: Archive or unarchive a product
admin_page: Products → (product name) → More actions → Archive product
page_summary: Archiving takes a product off your online store but keeps it in your admin so you can bring it back later. It's the safer choice when you might sell an item again. Archived products are listed under the Archived tab.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product.
2. Click More actions, then Archive product, and confirm in the dialog.
3. To restore it, go to the Archived tab in Products and open the product.
4. Click More actions, then Unarchive product, and confirm. The product comes back as a draft.

title: Delete one or more products
admin_page: Products → (product name) → More actions → Delete product
page_summary: Deleting removes a product from Shopify permanently, and it can't be undone or restored. If you might sell the item again, archive it instead.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product you want to remove.
2. Click More actions, then Delete product.
3. Confirm by clicking Delete product in the dialog.
4. To remove several products at once, tick their checkboxes on the Products list, choose the bulk action to delete the selected products, and confirm.

title: Add variants (size, color and other options)
page_summary: Variants let one product come in different versions, such as sizes or colors, each with its own price and stock. A product can have up to 3 options and up to 2,048 variants.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product.
2. In the Variants section, click Add options like size or color.
3. Type an option name, such as Size, then enter each value, such as Small, Medium and Large.
4. Optional: add a second or third option, such as Color.
5. Click Done, then Save, and set the prices for the new variants.

title: Edit or delete a variant
page_summary: Each variant has its own details page for its options, pricing, inventory and shipping. Quick changes to a variant's price or image can also be made from the product page.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product.
2. In the Variants section, click the variant you want to change.
3. Update its options, pricing, inventory or shipping, then click Save.
4. To remove the variant, click Delete variant on its page and confirm.
5. If you'll stop selling a variant but want to keep it, change where it's published instead of deleting it.
keywords: edit variant, change variant price, variant image, delete variant, remove variant, update variant, variant details

title: Create a collection
page_summary: Collections group products so customers can find them more easily, such as by category or for a sale. Products can be added automatically with conditions (for example, by tag or type), picked by hand, or a mix of both. You can also exclude products, and exclusions always take priority.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Collections.
2. Click Add collection and give it a title. Optionally add a description and a featured image.
3. In the Products source, either add conditions so matching products join automatically, or click Add products to pick items by hand. With more than one condition, choose whether products must match any or all of them.
4. Optional: exclude products, choose a sort order and pick the sales channels.
5. Click Save, then add the collection to your online store menu so customers can find it.
keywords: collection, create collection, add collection, category, group products, automated collection, smart collection, manual collection, conditions, exclude products

title: Manual collections (legacy collection type)
page_summary: If your admin still uses the older collection types, you choose between a manual collection, where you pick each product yourself, and a smart (automated) collection, which adds products based on conditions. An automated collection can't be turned into a manual one, so you'd need to create a new manual collection instead.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Collections and click Add collection.
2. Enter a title and description.
3. In the Collection type section, choose Manual, then click Save.
4. In the Products section, search or browse for products and add them. Then set the sort order.
5. Click Save. To add more products later, open the collection, add them in the Products section and save.
keywords: manual collection, smart collection, automated collection, collection type, add products to collection, legacy collections

title: Turn on inventory tracking (Track quantity)
page_summary: Turning on inventory tracking lets Shopify count stock for a product or variant and update it as items sell. Tracking is set separately for each variant. You can also decide whether customers can keep buying after stock reaches zero.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product. If it has variants, click the variant you want to track.
2. In the Inventory section, turn on Track quantity.
3. Optional: under Sell when out of stock, choose to keep selling when stock runs out.
4. Enter how many units are available.
5. Click Save. Repeat for each variant you want to track.
keywords: track quantity, inventory tracking, track stock, stock count, enable inventory, sell when out of stock, continue selling, oversell, backorder

title: View inventory levels
page_summary: The Inventory page lists every variant at each active location, with stock counts by state. Available is ready to sell, Committed is reserved for orders, Unavailable is on hand but not for sale, On hand is your total physical stock, and Incoming is stock arriving from transfers or purchase orders.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Inventory.
2. Optional: open the view menu (All) and choose a saved view.
3. Use the search bar to search for products, or add filters such as product type, vendor, tag or quantity.
4. Optional: open the columns (layout) icon to show, hide or reorder columns, or to change the sort.
keywords: inventory page, stock levels, view stock, available, on hand, committed, incoming, unavailable, inventory list, stock report

title: View inventory adjustment history
admin_page: Products → (product name) → Inventory → View adjustment history
page_summary: Adjustment history records each change to a tracked product's stock, including when it happened, what caused it and who or what made it. It's useful for tracing stock differences. The product page shows the last 180 days. For older records, use the Inventory adjustment changes report.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product.
2. If it has variants, click the variant you want to check. History is shown for one variant at a time.
3. In the Inventory section, make sure inventory tracking is on.
4. Click View adjustment history.
5. Review each entry's date, activity, who made the change and how the quantities changed.
keywords: inventory history, adjustment history, stock history, who changed inventory, inventory log, stock changes, audit inventory, missing stock

title: Transfer inventory between locations
page_summary: Transfers move stock between your locations, or to and from outside locations such as suppliers. You can track stock while it's moving and receive full or partial shipments. A new transfer is saved as a draft and doesn't move any stock until you process it.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Transfers and click Create transfer.
2. Choose the origin and destination locations. Leave one blank if it's an outside supplier or location.
3. Search for the products you want, add them, and enter a quantity for each in the Move column.
4. Optional: add a reference name, note or tags, then click Save to create a draft.
5. Open the transfer to mark it as ready to ship, in transit or transferred. Receiving stock doesn't make the product sellable at that location automatically.
keywords: transfer, inventory transfer, move stock, move inventory, between locations, warehouse transfer, restock store, ship to location

title: Create a purchase order
page_summary: A purchase order records what you're buying from a supplier, including products, quantities, costs and payment terms. Receiving the goods is tracked on a linked inventory transfer. Before starting, you need a supplier, a location to receive the stock and inventory tracking turned on for the products.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Purchase orders and click Create purchase order.
2. Choose a supplier, or create a new one. Optionally set the destination location.
3. Add products, then enter a quantity for each. Optionally add the supplier SKU and cost.
4. Optional: add a reference number, note, payment terms, supplier currency or tags. Review the cost summary, then click Save as draft.
5. Once the supplier confirms, click Mark as ordered. This can't be undone. Then create an inventory transfer to track the shipment.
keywords: purchase order, PO, supplier order, reorder stock, restock, order from supplier, vendor order, buy inventory

title: Sell gift cards (gift card product)
page_summary: A gift card product lets customers buy gift cards from your store in amounts you set. Each amount must be above zero and can be at most 10,000 USD or the local equivalent. Customers can't type in their own amount on the online store.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Gift cards.
2. Click Add a gift card product.
3. Enter a title, description and images, and choose the currency and sales channels. The cross-currency redemption setting can't be changed later.
4. Edit the amounts (denominations): replace the defaults, add new ones or remove ones you don't need. At least one is required.
5. Click Save gift card product.

title: Create and send a gift card
page_summary: You can create a gift card yourself in the admin and send it to a customer, for example as a reward or a goodwill gesture. The starting value can be at most 2,000 USD or the local equivalent. The code is generated for you.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Gift cards and click Create gift card.
2. Optional: choose the currency and the cross-currency redemption setting. This setting can't be changed later.
3. Enter the initial value, and pick or create the customer. They need an email address or phone number to receive it.
4. Optional: set an expiration date and add an internal note.
5. Click Save, then Send gift card, and choose to send it by email or SMS.

title: Manage existing gift cards
page_summary: Each gift card has a details page showing its starting and current balance, customer, order, expiry date and activity timeline. From there you can change the expiry date, resend the card or deactivate it. You can't edit a balance directly in the admin.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, go to Products → Gift cards.
2. Click the gift card you want to manage.
3. To change the expiry, click Edit expiry date, choose a new date and click Save.
4. To send it to the customer again, click Resend gift card. Only the remaining balance is sent.
5. To stop it from being used, click Deactivate. This is permanent and can't be reversed.

title: Import products from a CSV file
page_summary: A CSV import adds or updates many products at once from a spreadsheet file. The file can be up to 15 MB. Export your products first as a backup, because an import can't be canceled once it starts.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click Import.
2. Click Add file and choose your CSV. It should be saved with UTF-8 encoding.
3. Optional: clear the option to publish new products to all sales channels.
4. Optional: choose to overwrite products with matching handles. Blank optional columns will then clear existing values.

title: Export products to a CSV file
page_summary: Exporting saves your product data as a CSV file. You can use it as a backup, edit products in a spreadsheet or move them elsewhere. Depending on what you export, the file downloads in your browser or is sent by email.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click Export.
2. Choose what to export: the current page, all products, selected products, or products matching your search and filters.
3. Choose the file type: a CSV for spreadsheet apps such as Excel or Numbers, or a plain CSV.
4. Click Export products.
5. Exports of all products or filtered results are emailed to you. Smaller exports may download directly.

title: Bulk edit products
page_summary: The bulk editor shows the products you select in a spreadsheet-style table, so you can change many fields at once. For very large updates, a CSV import is better. Inventory for products with multiple variants has to be bulk edited from the Inventory page instead.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products.
2. Tick the checkboxes next to the products you want to change.
3. Click Bulk edit.
4. Optional: click Columns to add or remove fields such as price, SKU or tags.
5. Click a cell and type the new value, then click Save. If errors appear, fix them and save again.
keywords: bulk edit, edit multiple products, mass edit, bulk update prices, edit many products, spreadsheet editor, bulk actions

title: Add, reorder or remove product images and media
page_summary: The Media section of a product holds its images, videos and 3D models, with up to 250 items per product. The first item is the featured image shown in collections, the cart and checkout. Removing media from a product doesn't delete the file from your store.
steps:
1. In your Shopify admin, open Products and click the product.
2. In the Media section, click Upload new, drag files in, or click Select existing to reuse a file or add one from a URL.
3. To change the main image, drag it into the first position.
4. To remove items, tick their checkboxes and click Remove.
5. Save the product. To delete a file completely, remove it under Content → Files.

title: Show a sale price with compare-at price
page_summary: The compare-at price is the original price shown next to a lower selling price, so customers can see they're getting a sale. It must be higher than the price for the sale to show. Your theme decides how it looks, and checkout shows only the sale price.
steps:
